description: A conversation: an AI assistant whose replies run the full width, or people messaging in bubbles, with names, avatars, times in the app's locale, sent and read states, day dividers and a typing indicator. Opens at the newest message with no flash, keeps the reader's place when one arrives while they're scrolled up, and loads older messages from your endpoint as they scroll to the top. The composer grows with its text, sends on Enter, attaches files as chips (picking more adds to them; images show a preview), and takes suggested prompts. Files show as images or download cards. Screen readers hear new messages as they come. compact sizes it for a narrow column, at a sidebar's 14px. Works inside Livewire components, wire:stream included.

consider.note: Authorize the conversation on every route: the page, `history-url` and sending. The id in the URL can be changed to any other.

Attachments: the paperclip's `accept` only steers the picker. Check type and size in your Form Request, store under your own name on a private disk, and send them back as downloads, never SVG or HTML opened from your site.
For an AI assistant, show replies with `ChatMarkdown` or `{{ }}`, never as raw HTML: what a model writes can be steered by a page or file it read.
Load history a page at a time (20 is a good start) with `history-url`, never the whole conversation, from an index on `(conversation_id, id)`; `cursorPaginate()` keeps old pages fast.

Throttle sending. For an AI assistant, each message is a paid model call: consider a per-user daily limit, a cap on the reply's length, and sending the model only the recent messages, not the whole history.
For new messages from others, consider broadcasting (Reverb, Pusher) over polling: polling every few seconds is a request per open tab, all day.
